title: Pointers & memory
description: Loads, stores, and indirection in 64-bit mode
theory:
### Addresses with `lea` versus `mov`

**`lea reg, [base + index*scale + disp]`** computes an address without accessing memory.
**`mov reg, [addr]`** dereferences. Confusing the two is like mixing up **`&x`** and **`x`**:
both are legitimate, but only one loads the value.

Pointer-sized quantities are **64 bits** (`qword`). When you store an address of a label,
use **`dq label`** in **`.data`** and load it with **`mov rax, qword [rel ptr]`**.

### Stores and reloads

```nasm
section .bss
    slot: resb 1
section .data
    pslot: dq slot
section .text
    mov rax, qword [rel pslot]
    mov byte [rax], 'Z'
```

### Aliasing and TBAs

Two pointers that resolve to the same address alias the same memory. The CPU will happily
perform stores you did not logically expect if you computed two different paths to one
backing object—exactly why higher-level languages spend so much effort modeling aliasing.

exercises.title: Dereference byte
exercises.description: `.data` defines `x: db 'Q'` and `p: dq x` (pointer to `x`). Load `p` into `rax`, then print the byte at `[rax]` (`Q`, no newline), exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
x: db 'Q'
p: dq x
section .text
_start:
    ; mov rax, [rel p] then write one byte at [rax]
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `mov rax, qword [rel p]` then `mov rsi, rax` for `write`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
x: db 'Q'
p: dq x
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, qword [rel p]
    mov r8, rax
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, r8
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Store through pointer
exercises.description: Reserve one byte in `.bss` at `slot`. Let `ptr` in `.data` be `dq slot`. Store `'Z'` into `slot` **through** `ptr` (two-step: load ptr to reg, `mov byte [reg], 'Z'`). Print `slot` with one-byte `write`, exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .bss
slot: resb 1
section .data
ptr: dq slot
section .text
_start:
    ; mov rax, [rel ptr]; mov byte [rax], 'Z'
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .bss
slot: resb 1
section .data
ptr: dq slot
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, qword [rel ptr]
    mov byte [rax], 'Z'
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel slot]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Pointer arithmetic
exercises.description: Array `db 'M','N','O'`. Let `base` hold its address (`dq arr`). Load pointer, add **2** to point at `'O'`, print that single byte, exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'M','N','O'
base: dq arr
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'M', 'N', 'O'
base: dq arr
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, qword [rel base]
    add rax, 2
    mov r8, rax
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, r8
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Base + index byte
exercises.description: Array `db 'J','K','L'` at `arr`. Put `lea rbx, [rel arr]` in `rbx`, then load the middle byte with `movzx eax, byte [rbx+1]`. Store that ASCII byte into one-byte `.bss` `out`, `write` `out`, exit 0. Expected stdout (trimmed) is `K`.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'J','K','L'
section .bss
out: resb 1
section .text
_start:
    ; lea rbx, [rel arr]; movzx eax, byte [rbx+1]; mov [out], al; write
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `movzx` widens the byte so you can use a 32-bit `add` later if needed — here storing `al` is enough
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
arr: db 'J', 'K', 'L'
section .bss
out: resb 1
section .text
_start:
    lea rbx, [rel arr]
    movzx eax, byte [rbx+1]
    mov [rel out], al
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel out]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
